elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer (no prohibition on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products)
elements.evidence: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."

elements.element: No field-of-use / territorial restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: No surviving post-term restrictive covenant (e.g. 24-month tail)
elements.evidence: the 24-month tail now attaches only to a permission: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire"

elements.element: Restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: no restriction remains; clause reads "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service"
"During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" retained, but as a permission not a restriction

elements.element: Carve-out for internal development and acquisitions

reasons: The single operator change ("shall not" → "may") removes the non-compete entirely, satisfying the locked preferred position that no non-compete or field-of-use restriction bind Customer.
Minimal: one short phrase replaced; no fallback mechanics (named product, 12-month cap, carve-outs) were imported and no clause rewrite occurred.

Intent preserved: § 12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement remains effective and § 12.4 now reads consistently with it as a permission; no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced. The retained "twenty-four months thereafter" wording is redundant in a permission but not contradictory.
